record_notes.DCP-LETT-2180: December 4, supplied 1857, six blocks and complete notes/bibliography read. Returns Candolle and two pamphlets this day, Thuret particularly useful; tables enclosed for opinion but full tables not transcribed. Requests hot/dry garden contacts and lost former humidity reference, not already having those answers. P2/P5 ask for Henslow news; final P6 explicitly acknowledges note just received answering that request, matching 2178. Receipt occurs during composition, so only final P6 is reply to this incoming note; earlier questions must not be recast as informed by it. Exact December 4 receipt supported; no clock time. Thuret reciprocal-cross failure is editorial quotation of later manuscript, not separate incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2181: Incomplete Hooker letter, Sunday assigned December 6, 1857, nine blocks, annotations, all notes and bibliography read. Candolle results interesting, orders may be grouped with Proteaceae separate due local distribution. Labiatae well delimited, large and widespread, thus substantial counterexample. Asks global and local floras with differing species criteria; Rubus varies by region, a local variety may disappear in a worldwide treatment. Bentham manuscript done, publication expected Easter, not already published; Decaisne report attributed. P6 Linum alternate upper leaves qualified and illegible phrase retained. Missing 2156 query sheet not reconstructed; footnote 11 quotes Hooker answer and says he drew a diagram, but no actual diagram present in this source. Cucubalus list sent, full list absent. P8 names Mueller and Moore, allows Hooker names, gives qualified assessments and predicted Mueller 1859 return, no completed journey. P9 moisture point. Undated Darwin markings separate. Answers 2180 referral request and solicited review; 2182 directly responds. Mueller introduction used by December 8 in 2378.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2182: December 9, supplied 1857, eight blocks and all notes/bibliography read. Explicitly thanks Candolle opinion, requests more volumes for December 16. P2 disagrees that global monographs are best for his particular question, gives geographic genus-size reasoning while anticipating rule may hold both scales. P3 proposes retesting Labiatae, P4 acknowledges serious blow despite many favorable floras; not denial of counterexample. P5 Bentham/Silene thanks corresponds forwarded list, P6 Mueller and Moore letters now written. P7 so-few-aids phrase absent from surviving incomplete 2181; do not restore missing ending from response. Later six-volume analysis and inability to incorporate Bentham 1858 are apparatus, not completed December 9. Direct reply scope P1–6.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2188: Hooker letter assigned December 17–23, 1857, five blocks and complete annotations/notes/bibliography read. Forgot requested December 16 book dispatch, now promises Thursday carrier; date window not exact dispatch or receipt. Labiatae anomaly and Bentham over-splitting conjecture, extent unknown. Begun Tasmania introduction and plans descriptive account without conclusions, not finished or published work. Over 100 European plants near Melbourne naturalized is attributed report. Two Gray tracts sent by post, editorial identities probable, not both proved solely by bundle. Dana metaphysics question is distinctive surviving prompt. Undated Darwin crossings separate. Reverse acknowledgement of 2182 loan request; direct prompt for 2194.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2194: December 25, supplied 1857, eleven blocks and all notes/bibliography read. Book arrival explicitly this morning; letter arrival not separately dated. Candolle analysis future long job, Brown Prodromus received, Labiatae retest later. P6 Dana pamphlet read and criticized with attributed J. E. Gray phrase, Darwin conjecture about Dana Genesis belief not independent fact. P7 reading Huxley proof sheets, not finished reading or printed 1865 catalogue already published. P8 specifically answers Hooker intended non-generalizing Tasmania introduction. P2 concerns separate Mrs Hooker note; P9 Henslow question and P11 chapter progress separate. P11 says hybridism chapter just finished after three months, whereas journal apparatus says December 29; preserve version/stage discrepancy without redating whole December 25 letter. Worker proposal 2194→2170 joins Darwin outgoing letters and reverses book custody: 2170 planned return of older loans, 2194 receives new loans following 2188.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2378: Additional Darwin-to-Mueller December 8 with year supplied, two blocks, full notes/bibliography read. Uses William and Joseph Hooker names as introduction, asks whether British/northern European perennials can live and set seed in hot southern Australia, controlling competing native plants and possibly watering; southern European success only presupposed. Naturalized British plants partly answer question, enumeration requested, not received. Later missing Mueller reply cited in manuscript is not surviving input or already known here. Specific Hooker December 6 recommendation and introduction permission demonstrably used by December 8, before December 9 direct answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2170: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 14 with month/year supplied from planned London visit and prior Moor Park stay, six blocks and all apparatus/bibliography read. Remaining books to be sent Tuesday November 17, not already delivered; requests Candolle/Lowe/shell book (body says Hancock, apparatus Hanley), ownership or reading not inferred. Adlumia seeds received, observation future. P3 Coe letter and mixed beans received; distinctive first-generation coat/size change, sowing next year prospective. Source 2165 November 4 supports knowledge by November 14. Coe 2171 acknowledges missing Darwin November 13 thanks, an earlier indirect clue without surviving Darwin body. Medals note expressly burned, prompt missing; Lindley award future November 30, Lyell 1858 outcome later. Reported personal rest benefit not a medical generalization.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2174: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 21, supplied 1857, three blocks, notes and bibliography read. Missing Hooker note reports Harriet Henslow dangerously ill; Darwin writes conditionally if worst happens and remembers Cambridge kindness. Actual death occurred November 20 per later apparatus, but body does not show Darwin knew it on November 21. Requests brief news of Henslow and says he will not trouble him directly. Hooker 2178 P1–2 supplies family report and acknowledges loving words; reverse link supported, forwarding mechanics uncertain.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2178: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Wednesday assigned December 2, 1857, seven blocks, annotations and bibliography read. Returned Monday from Hitcham, wife stayed. Henslow grief and family work reported; Harriet peaceful death, no pain last twelve hours. Appreciates Darwin affectionate words. First rough Impatiens monograph: 100 Indian species, few extra-Indian, very local species and little marked variation. Editorial summary overstates endemism and says over 100. Later 1859 claim of excessive variation differs and must not be backdated. Remaining query answers future, others cannot answer. Livingstone cucumber report is attributed reading, not Hooker experiment. Lindley applause refers November 30 event. Darwin pencil crossings undated. Darwin December 4 reply belongs next packet.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
